requires.hardware: Python 3.11+ and standard library for the host reference; backend hardware is an engine choice
requires.model: Caller-serializable state with an explicit compatibility fingerprint and codec
requires.workload: Repeated compatible prefixes with enough reuse to amortize serialization and reads

contract.input: Caller-owned cache directory, immutable state fingerprint and bundle/component codecs, semantic prefix bytes and exact bounded opaque components; transfer parts, staging/pump quotas, leased sources and private destinations
contract.output: Checksum-verified Checkpoint, validated RestorePlan or complete PublishedBundle with private destination owners
contract.ownership: Storage owns immutable encoded records. Restore transactions retain all source, destination, reader, receipt and callback owners through settlement; active/failed work has bounded strong retention. Native callbacks own partial failures.
contract.failure: Bundle decoding rejects incomplete/incompatible components, codec/extent/digest errors and overflow before destination allocation. Streaming transport hashes incrementally into private destinations and fails on short I/O or digest mismatch. Copy/reader failure never publishes partial state; ambiguous submission or settlement retains the complete transaction until explicit backend proof.
contract.core_boundary: Restore into a separately owned consumer state only after byte/codec validation; core still owns the live request lifetime.

validation.host: Host fixtures and examples cover exact/longest lookup, immutable identities, complete components, capacity/corruption, private publication, pending readers, failures and split-source leases; transfer tests cover staged file copies, byte/callback quotas, backpressure, reordered completion, cancelled/failed/short I/O, incremental digests and retained unknown work; admission tests cover source gates, tier costs, recomputation and capture boundaries; 400 prefix intersections against explicit sets; heterogeneous alignment/overflow checks; real host tier copies, source/destination races, delayed readers, capacity, corruption and ambiguous submission retention; live queued decisions, aggregate quotas, deadline fallback, source/destination races, corruption and retained cancelled/ambiguous readers
validation.native: Native state restoration, crash durability and model continuation remain unqualified by host fixtures
validation.performance: Unmeasured for a native engine; host fixture success is not a speed claim
